name: Vistabel

lead: Vistabel is the European trade name of the botulinum toxin type A product sold as Botox Cosmetic by Allergan. It is used to soften glabellar ("frown") lines between the eyebrows by relaxing the muscles that create them.

It appeals to people who want a smoother, less tense-looking upper face. Randomised and dose-ranging studies, including trials in men and of forehead and eyebrow position, have examined it for lines and brow shape.

paras: Administered by a clinician as small injections into targeted facial muscles. Smoothing is usually visible within days and lasts a few months, after which treatment can be repeated. Practitioners also use it in the forehead and crow's-feet areas.

Reported effects include bruising, headache and unintended weakness of nearby muscles, such as eyelid or brow drooping. It is a prescription medicine and is used under medical supervision; this entry does not cover dosing.

chain: Toxin blocks muscle signal in the frown area
angle.text: Injected into the frown muscles, it temporarily relaxes them so glabellar lines look softer; forehead dosing also affects brow position.

lead: Vistabel is the name under which onabotulinumtoxinA, Allergan's botulinum toxin type A, is marketed for cosmetic use in Europe; in the United States the equivalent is Botox Cosmetic.[1][2] It is used to reduce glabellar lines by temporarily relaxing the muscles between the brows.[2]

For appearance, it softens frown lines and, depending on where it is injected, can alter brow position and the look of the forehead or crow's feet.[3][4] Researchers have studied it in men and in dose-response designs for glabellar lines, forehead rhytides and crow's feet.[5][3]
Botox Cosmetic received FDA approval in 2002 for moderate-to-severe glabellar lines, with effects typically lasting two to four months.[6]

paras: The primary indication is glabellar lines. Reviews describe onabotulinumtoxinA and abobotulinumtoxinA as effective and well tolerated for facial aesthetic procedures.[2]

Other studied sites include the forehead, where a prospective study of 24 patients treated with Vistabel examined wrinkle reduction and eyebrow position, and the lateral eye area for crow's feet.[3][4] A jawline re-contouring technique using botulinum toxin, the "Nefertiti lift", has also been described.[7]

A randomised, double-blind, dose-ranging study in 80 men compared four total doses for glabellar rhytids, assessing safety, efficacy and duration of response.[5] A placebo-controlled dose-response trial examined crow's feet.[4] A French study of forehead injections measured wrinkle reduction and eyebrow modification.[3]

A meta-analysis compared the relative potency of incobotulinumtoxinA and onabotulinumtoxinA (Botox/Vistabel).[8] A comparative review addressed effectiveness and economic impact of type A toxins for aesthetic indications.[9]

Cosmetic botulinum toxin products include Botox Cosmetic/Vistabel (Allergan), Dysport/Azzalure, Xeomin/Bocouture and Jeuveau/Nuceiva. Differences in formulation and unit definitions mean units are not interchangeable between brands.[6][1]
Reported effects include injection-site bruising, headache, flu-like symptoms, and unintended weakness of nearby muscles; eyelid or brow drooping has been reported with cosmetic toxins.[6]
